findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm e27c's 'bridge_fsck unchanged' scope (CLI verb rename + schema $id/description text) is disjoint from 030f's output-contract change (removed keys + store_integrity), that 030f lands strictly after e27c, and that bridge_fsck.schema.json edits from both children compose without contradicting either child's contract tests.
evidence: e27c AC: 'The library and MCP `bridge_fsck` entrypoints are UNCHANGED by this ticket and still callable at its boundary'
e27c: 'This ticket renames the CLI verb and updates the shared JSON-schema text only.'

030f Decision 1: 'Remove `orphaned`, `duplicates`, and `stale` from the structured output and human report. ... Update every consumer in the same shippable change: `rebar.bridge_fsck`, generated `BridgeFsck` and `BridgeFsckOut`, the JSON schema, MCP validation ...'
Roster note: 030f depends_on e27c (030f edits bridge_fsck, which e27c renames)
findings.finding: The bridge_fsck result/output contract is described from opposite directions by two dependency-linked siblings without an explicit reconciled handoff: e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2 asserts the library/MCP bridge_fsck entrypoints (and, at its boundary, the CLI's shared schema behavior) are UNCHANGED and merely renamed, whereas 030f-c14f-596a-4f79 rewrites that same bridge_fsck output contract — removing orphaned/duplicates/stale and adding store_integrity/unknown_event_types/binding_drift across the TypedDict, JSON schema, MCP model, and CLI probe.
scenarios: A reviewer verifying e27c's 'bridge_fsck unchanged' AC after 030f has landed will see the result contract changed, creating apparent inconsistency between the two closed children's claims.

The shared bridge_fsck.schema.json is edited by both e27c ($id/description rename) and 030f (six-value store_integrity enum, removed keys); if landed out of the depends_on order the schema-coverage/output/MCP contract tests could diverge.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit cross-reference in e27c narrowing 'unchanged' to 'the callable boundary and shared schema TEXT only, while the output-key contract change is owned by 030f which lands after this rename', and confirm the schema-edit ordering in the depends_on chain.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the ADR index/numbering gate (docs/adr/README.md, check_adr_numbers.py, gen_adr_index.py) is regenerated consistently across the 0092 (4a44), 0094 (b69c), and 0070-amend (e27c) changes so no collision or out-of-index entry survives any landing order.
evidence: 4a44 AC: 'ADR 0092, its reservation marker, generated index, architecture link, and release link pass the current ADR numbering/index checks'

b69c: 'ADR 0094 records ... Follow the current numbering convention with `docs/adr/.numbers/0094`, generated index, `check_adr_numbers.py`, and `gen_adr_index.py --check`; if origin/main claims 0094, allocate the next free four-digit number and regenerate references.'
e27c: 'Amend `docs/adr/0070-jira-onboard-config-write.md` ... the existing number marker and generated index remain authoritative and their checks must pass.'
findings.finding: The single shared ADR index/numbering gate (docs/adr/README.md, check_adr_numbers.py, gen_adr_index.py) is mutated by three siblings allocating/amending different ADR numbers, creating a shared-state interaction across children: 4a44 owns ADR 0092 (with its reservation marker and generated index), b69c owns ADR 0094 (with docs/adr/.numbers/0094 and index), and e27c amends ADR 0070. Each independently asserts the ADR index/collision checks pass.
scenarios: If two children each regenerate docs/adr/README.md and the .numbers markers independently, a merge/landing-order interleave could produce a transient index/collision-gate failure or an out-of-order index entry.
b69c's own guard ('if origin/main claims 0094, allocate the next free number') signals awareness of number-collision risk on the shared numbering namespace touched by 4a44 and b69c together.
findings.suggested_fix: Record an explicit ordering/regeneration note that whichever ADR change lands later re-runs gen_adr_index.py --check against the combined set, and verify 0092/0094 do not collide with any origin/main allocation.

findings.finding: Nine parent Portability acceptance criteria have no covering acceptance criterion among the 12 direct children in the roster. The named coordinator (child 2db2) delegates them to grandchildren 591d/8b08, which are NOT in the sibling roster; 2db2's own seven ACs cover only child-closure, legacy retention, the packaged runner via `rebar bridge run`, and the no-gh repair test. The specific uncovered/indeterminate criteria are: scrubbed-environment identical contract failing on vendor-variable reads or required gh (P1), full-depth success + named shallow-clone rejection for bug f193 (P2), Jenkinsfile and .gitlab-ci.yml committed and doc-referenced (P3), GHA 20-minute production workflow (P4), one code-derived exit/secret/timeout table (P5), single-quoted Jenkins Groovy body (P6), offline GitLab schema validation with recorded provenance (P7), pinned shellcheck over all three providers (P8), and CI shellcheck provisioning with named-failure-not-skip (P9).
findings.location: child 2db2-3f5e-cf3a-464c (Acceptance Criteria) vs parent 'Portability acceptance criteria' P1-P9
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit acceptance criteria to 2db2 (or surface 591d/8b08 in the roster) for each of P1-P9 so the union of direct children demonstrably delivers the scrubbed-env contract, shallow-clone rejection, committed+referenced Jenkinsfile/.gitlab-ci.yml, 20-min GHA, shared exit/secret/timeout table, single-quoted Groovy, offline GitLab schema validation, and pinned-shellcheck provisioning.

findings.finding: Parent main AC7 ('The bridge runs locally, on GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments') is only partially covered by the roster. Child 2db2 AC5 asserts that these five environments 'use the packaged Python core in src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py through exactly rebar bridge run', but no direct-child AC in the roster demonstrates the OBSERVABLE outcome that a bridge run actually SUCCEEDS end-to-end in each of the five environments (that observable is delegated to grandchildren 591d/8b08 absent from the roster).
findings.location: child 2db2-3f5e-cf3a-464c (AC5) vs parent main AC 'The bridge runs locally, on GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to 2db2 an acceptance criterion asserting the scrubbed-environment success/identity contract (or surface 591d in the roster) so main AC7's five-environment run-success is delivered at the direct-child level.
